properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-24 by Anthony: *"I kind of don't want to be dependent upon dynograph-foundation anymore"* and *"by absorbing, I don't mean all dynograph-foundation crates - I mean only the ones that are needed in reflow2."*

This CHOOSES among the options `dec:idea-cannibalize-dynograph-foundation-into-reflow2` costed and left open. That node stays as the record of the options; this one records the choice and the plan.

═══ 🛑 THE PLAN WAS CORRECTED 2026-08-24 — IT WAS FIVE INCREMENTS AND IT IS FOUR ═══

**As first written this decision promised "five increments, each independently shippable, stop after any of". That was true for 1, 2 and 3 and FALSE for 4 and 5.** The prior text is preserved at `snap:epoch:the-absorption:dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency`; the correction is `chg:increments-4-and-5-are-one-increment`.

WHY: `dynograph-storage/src/lib.rs:32` re-exports `pub use dynograph_core::{DynoError, Schema, Value}`, and `StoredNode.properties` is `HashMap<String, Value>` of that same type. Absorbing core while storage stays external gives reflow2 TWO distinct types called `Value` and TWO called `DynoError` — the in-tree ones, and the ones every `StorageEngine` call keeps returning. 48 files name `DynoError`, 33 name `Value`. Nothing compiles. No ordering avoids it: storage DEPENDS ON core, so it cannot go first.

⭐ HOW THE COSTING MISSED IT: it measured each crate's SIZE, each crate's IMPORT COUNT, and the dependency DIRECTION between crates. It never asked whether two crates share TYPES ACROSS the boundary. **A dependency graph tells you what needs what to build; it does not tell you what breaks if you take one and not the other.** Found by scouting before writing code — two import sites out of eighty-six, and the signal was two lines wide.

═══ WHY THE EARLIER RECOMMENDATION IS NO LONGER THE RIGHT ONE ═══

The brainstorm states the trap plainly: **"Two problems look like one here and have different answers. (a) DEAD WEIGHT ... (b) THE DEPENDENCY ITSELF ... Option C solves (a) and does nothing for (b)."** Option C was recommended and deferred. Anthony has now said which he is solving: **(b)**. C removes two crates from the manifest and leaves the dependency where it is. This is trimmed option A.

⭐ ITS REOPENING TRIGGERS WERE NOT WHAT REOPENED IT. The node named two — the pin-confirmation cost recurring, or reflow2 needing to CHANGE foundation behaviour. **Neither happened.** What reopened it is a third thing that node had already written as option D's counter: *"the reason for absorbing is not technical, it is about what reflow2 IS."* **A deferral's stated triggers are not the only way back in**, and a reader who treats them as exhaustive will hold a decision closed against its owner.

═══ IT STAYS INSIDE THE OWNERSHIP BOUND ═══

`dec:idea-dynograph-crates-independent-in-code-coupled-in-release` sets a bound this decision must respect: *"reflow2's design has no standing to decide [dynograph's structure] ... the only options reflow2 can weigh honestly on its own are A (accept it) and E (take less)."* **This is E, taken to its end.** Every step happens in reflow2's own repository, needs no upstream change, and decides nothing about dynograph-foundation's release structure, its other four crates, or its other consumers. That question stays open and stays theirs.

═══ THE MEASUREMENT THAT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE ═══

Measured 2026-08-24 at v0.12.0 (`b5a9f74`), file by file, from every `use dynograph_*` in reflow2 and the internal closure of what those names reach:

    crate                 needed    total    dead
    dynograph-core         1,941    1,941      0%   the whole type vocabulary
    dynograph-storage      2,728    2,836      4%   (+2,187 lines of its own tests)
    dynograph-text           847      847      0%   ⇐ NOT IN ANY EARLIER COUNT
    dynograph-graph        2,219    3,832     42%   ⇐ corrected from 1,844/52%
    dynograph-resolution     300    1,211     75%
    dynograph-vector         436    2,377     82%

⇒ **about +15% to reflow2's 53,005-line tree, not the +27% the all-crates figure implied.**

🛑 **SIX CRATES, NOT FIVE.** `dynograph-storage` depends on `dynograph-text` for the `fulltext` feature, and reflow2 USES fulltext. 847 lines, and it brings **tantivy 0.26**. No COSTING of the absorption ever counted it.

OTHER EXTERNAL CRATES INHERITED: `rmp-serde`, `lru`, `rand`, `serde_yaml`, `uuid`, `thiserror`, `tantivy`.

═══ WHAT REFLOW2 WOULD OWN FOREVER — the real cost, and it is not line count ═══

  ~2,700 lines of RocksDB storage engine (backend, keys, cache, engine/*)
    847 lines of tantivy-backed full-text index
    695 lines of Leiden community detection
  1,752 lines of schema engine (core/schema.rs)

═══ ONE RECORDED OBJECTION WEAKENS, ONE STANDS ═══

⭐ WEAKER — *"you lose the upstream's fixes silently."* **Upstream is Anthony's own repository.** No vendor, no third party. And storyflow keeps dynograph-foundation alive through its REST surface, which `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` measured as disjoint from reflow2's Rust-library surface. The repo does not die and storyflow is untouched; reflow2 stops linking it, that is all.

🛑 STANDS — *"Vendoring converts a visible dependency into an invisible one."* The pin carries a written reason for every bump; the v0.11→v0.12 note recording a `TextHit` type leak is real history with no successor once the code is in-tree. MITIGATION, required rather than optional: each increment records a ChangeEvent naming the exact TAG absorbed and the FILES taken, and each absorbed module carries a header saying the same.

═══ THE PLAN — FOUR increments ═══

  ✅ 1. VECTOR → `stats.rs` (436 lines, 1 importing file). SHIPPED, PR #326.
  ✅ 2. RESOLUTION → `fuzzy.rs` (300 lines, 3 files). SHIPPED, PR #327 — and it took
        dynograph-vector out of the BUILD GRAPH with it, discharging increment 1's caveat.
  ✅ 3. GRAPH → `graphalg/` (2,219 lines, 3 files). SHIPPED, PR #328.
        ⭐ ZERO new external dependencies. Dropped 1,613 lines in nine files.
  ⬜ 4. CORE + STORAGE + TEXT, TOGETHER AND NOT SEPARABLE (~5,516 lines, ~86 files).
        Brings rocksdb and tantivy. **THIS IS THE ONE THAT ENDS THE DEPENDENCY.**

⭐ AFTER 1-3 — reached 2026-08-24: three of six crates gone, ~2,955 lines moved, 7 files of
churn, and NO new external crate in the tree. **This is a genuine stopping point and it is the
LAST one.** Step 4 has no interior stopping point at all, which is precisely what the original
plan got wrong.

🛑 STEPS 1-3 SHRANK THE DEPENDENCY; ONLY STEP 4 ENDS IT. "We absorbed the foundation" said before
step 4 lands would be false.

═══ WHAT THIS DECIDES BY CONSTRUCTION, AND WHAT IT CANCELS ═══

`dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier` is answered by construction on completion: no supplier left to be. The five `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces are then RETIRED on the record — they were true — not deleted.

🛑 CANCELS mirroring dynograph's published surface into reflow2, dropped on Anthony's word the same day it was proposed: absorbing removes the seam a mirror would describe, so the two are ALTERNATIVES. The flo2 → reflow2 mirror is unaffected. Also moot: the v0.13.0 pin parked since 2026-08-19.
properties.name: DECIDED — absorb only what reflow2 needs from dynograph-foundation and end the dependency, in FOUR increments: three you can stop after, and a fourth that cannot be split
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own node rather than by editing the brainstorm, because that node's value is the OPTIONS and their costs and it should keep reading as where the thinking happened.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT LESSON, and it is the second time in one day: the earlier costing measured whole crates and stated honestly what it had not measured. Measuring the missing part changed the headline from +27% to +15% AND found a sixth crate (`dynograph-text`, and tantivy behind it) that no costing of this idea mentions. **A number that answers a narrower question than the one being asked is not evidence about the wider one** — the same shape as the edge-only shortlist measurement corrected earlier today, one level up.

🛑 A STALE PREMISE FOUND WHILE READING THE SIBLINGS, and it is not corrected here because correcting another node's text is a separate act: `dec:idea-dynograph-crates-independent-in-code-coupled-in-release` states that this decision is recorded in reflow2's graph "because dynograph-foundation has no reflow2 design of its own". **It has one.** Verified 2026-08-24 with `describe_designs`, which opens nothing: graph_id `dynograph-foundation`, origin `adopted`, minted by 0.16.0, with a committed 179-node export and a `docs/published-surface.json` carrying 15 published Interfaces. The premise was true when written and is false now.
